decisions.reason: The existing message-114 MODIFY already records the É accent's derivation from the selected Option 2 Hero V termination, including the terminal behavior and adjustment constraints.

The existing MODIFY captures the new terminal treatment but leaves the prior instruction to extend the right arm farther in state, despite the client's explicit instruction not to lengthen it during this refinement.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
The biggest change for me happened after our last conversation. When we stopped discussing only how the V should look and began considering whom it represents, it felt as though we finally started designing toward the same purpose. Your insightful questions made that possible, so thank you. The philosophy is genuinely visible in this round, and I appreciate the care with which you translated it.

My favorite is Option 2.

This may honestly be the V. Nothing else we have explored has felt this complete.

There is just one refinement I would still like to test: the very end of the right arm. Following it upward, I want the gesture to conclude with total conviction instead of gradually fading. It should not become longer, thicker, or more curved. The ending simply needs to feel slightly more intentional, as if it knows precisely where it is going.

That termination will eventually define more than the large V. It will also shape the smaller V and, most importantly, the É accent. Because the gesture is destined to become a defining signature of the Veillvé identity, it is worth considering whether it communicates the same quiet confidence and sense of becoming that the brand represents.

value_updates.terminal_conclusion: intentional and decisive rather than gradually fading
value_updates.terminal_expression: The shared terminal should communicate quiet confidence and a sense of becoming.

decisions.reason: Selecting Option 2 as the near-final V and requesting only one terminal refinement makes the prior instruction to explore several fundamentally different directions obsolete.

decisions.reason: The source changes the shared geometric terminal, not the deferred champagne-metal material treatment or its sequencing and role.
Quiet confidence and becoming are existing brand-expression principles used to evaluate the terminal; the source does not change those principles.
The source applies the terminal to the Hero V, smaller V, and É accent and does not change the deferred construction of the remaining proprietary letterforms.
The terminal refinement does not change the deferred complete-wordmark kerning, rhythm, or visual hierarchy.
Refining the shared V-system terminal does not alter the decision to use a proprietary wordmark without a separate icon or monogram.
